subject: Priority lane crediting & escalation routing — commercial terms request
messages:
From: Chris Nolan <chris.nolan@acmeanalytics.com>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acmeanalytics.com
Date: Thu, 19 Aug 2026 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Priority lane crediting & escalation routing — initial Qs

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the product walkthrough yesterday — the performance looked good. Before we take this to procurement I need a clearer read on how you price the SLA + premium support. Two areas in particular:

1) "Priority lane" crediting: you mentioned prefix caching and a priority lane that reduces queueing for our critical flows. How does that translate to credits/penalties when availability dips? Do you measure credits against the single combined endpoint or per-model?

2) Escalation routing / on-call coverage: we have strict requirements for 24x7 escalation during launch. What does Redwood consider "escalation coverage" (dedicated on-call vs pooled rotation), and is there a way to purchase a guaranteed routing path to specific engineers?

We are evaluating a 12‑month commit and would like to understand the discount bands if we: (a) commit to >= $250k ARR, and (b) take a 24/7 escalation add-on. Our procurement team is pushing for a 15% list-level discount if we take both. Can you confirm what you can offer and share any paperwork/appendix we can attach to the PO?

Appreciate a short note — happy to hop on a 20-minute call if easier.

Thanks,
Chris
Chris Nolan
Head of Platform Engineering
Acme Analytics

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.inference.com>
To: Chris Nolan <chris.nolan@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.inference.com, jordan.blake@redwood.inference.com
Date: Thu, 19 Aug 2026 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Priority lane crediting & escalation routing — initial Qs

Hi Chris — thanks for the thoughtful questions. Quick answers below and I've attached an SLA appendix and a pricing workbook for the ACME sizing you mentioned.

1) Priority lane crediting:
- How measured: credits are issued per-route (logical endpoint) not per-model; for mixed-model routes we treat the route as the unit for SLO measurement.
- When queueing impacts observed latency beyond the SLO, we first offset with automated burst capacity and prefix cache hits; credits are applied only when the burst+cache cannot restore the SLO within the measurement window.
- Credit banding: for availability we use tiered slabs (>=99.95%, 99.9–99.95%, <99.9%) with escalating credit percentages. For priority-lane degradation (e.g., observed elevated tail latency for priority-tagged requests) we apply a separate latency-crediting formula in the appendix.

2) Escalation routing / on-call:
- Default: pooled regional rotation with guaranteed tier‑1 triage within the response window.
- Dedicated path: for an add-on, we can provide a scoped routing path that maps your critical routes to a named on-call rotation (not a named engineer, but a dedicated team with priority paging). This includes a private Slack channel and a 24x7 pager for severe incidents.
- Guaranteed engineer routing (named-point) can be done but it requires an on-call retainer (see pricing workbook) to cover capacity and partial seat allocation.

Commercial note: the pricing workbook I attached models three options: standard (no retainer), retainer-lite (4 dedicated on‑call hours/month + priority lane), and retainer-plus (8 hours/month + 24x7 escalation + faster SLA windows). For a 12‑month $250k commit:
- We can commit to an 8% list discount at $250k ARR with retainer-lite.
- Retainer-plus unlocks up to 12% discount and expanded operational guarantees.

We can't commit to a blanket 15% at that commitment level unless there's an expanded multiyear commit or a separate enterprise package (which Jordan can scope).

Next steps: if you want to see updated language for procurement, I can circulate a short addendum (SLA appendix + pricing workbook) that you can attach to the PO. Also include the DocuSign link for the MA if you prefer signatures rather than a PO.

I'll leave Jordan on copy for any escalations on discounts. If you'd like, we can run a 30-day pilot of the priority lane at a reduced retainer to validate metrics before sign.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: Redwood_SLA_Appendix_v2.pdf, ACME_MA-pricing-v3.xlsx, PriorityLane-FAQ.txt

From: Chris Nolan <chris.nolan@acmeanalytics.com>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.inference.com
Cc: procurement@acmeanalytics.com
Date: Thu, 19 Aug 2026 12:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Priority lane crediting & escalation routing — initial Qs

Tessa — thanks for the clear breakdown and attachments. A couple of follow-ups after we've reviewed the appendix:

- Escalation coverage: our launch window is mission critical (global retail customers) — we need named escalation routing if possible. I get that "named engineer" is expensive; would Redwood accept a compromise where you provide a named escalation lead (SPOC) during the 90-day launch period and then revert to dedicated team rotation?

- Discounting: procurement is firm on 15% as the threshold for the $250k commit to sign quickly. If you can't meet 15% at $250k, would Redwood accept an 8% discount at $250k with a guaranteed path to 15% (retroactive) if we hit $400k within 6 months? That gives us runway to expand.

- Pilot: we'd be open to the 30-day pilot but need a trial SLA that actually measures priority-lane tail latency and a clear success threshold. If Redwood can agree to named escalation lead during the pilot and a written path to retroactive increases on discount, we can expedite sign-off on our end.

Can you outline that in writing (short bullets) so I can share with our GC and procurement?

--
Chris

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.inference.com>
To: Chris Nolan <chris.nolan@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.inference.com, jordan.blake@redwood.inference.com
Date: Thu, 19 Aug 2026 14:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Priority lane crediting & escalation routing — initial Qs

Chris — appreciate the specificity; here's a short, procurement-friendly summary you can paste into the PO or email to GC: 

1) Pilot and named escalation lead:
- 30‑day pilot: Redwood will enable the priority lane for the scoped routes in the workbook and measure tail-latency (p95/p99) and hit-rate for prefix caching.
- Named escalation lead: for the 30‑day pilot + 90‑day launch window, Redwood will assign a named escalation lead (Sr. Oncall Engineer) as a single SPOC for critical incidents. The lead will coordinate with our rotation but is explicitly assigned to ACME for the agreed period.

2) Discounting & retroactive uplift path:
- Base 12‑month commitment at $250k ARR: 8% list discount with retainer-lite (4 hours/month).
- Performance-based uplift: if ACME reaches $400k ARR within the first 6 months, Redwood will apply a retroactive uplift to 15% for the period starting at contract effective date (subject to standard audit verification).

3) Procurement attachments and DocuSign:
- Attached: Redwood_SLA_Appendix_v2.pdf (defines priority-lane credits and latency measurement), ACME_MA-pricing-v3.xlsx (line-item pricing), PriorityLane-FAQ.txt.
- We can produce a 1‑page addendum for your PO that references the pilot scope and the retroactive uplift path; once you confirm procurement contact I will route the DocuSign envelope.

If that works, Ben will draft the addendum and Jordan will review discount approvals. I can push the DocuSign to procurement for signature the same day we get your go‑ahead.

Next actions (suggested):
- You: confirm procurement contact and pilot routes (list of endpoints) by EOD 8/20.
- Redwood: Ben will draft the addendum; Tessa will open the DocuSign envelope; Jordan will confirm discount uplift routing.

Would you like a 15-minute call this afternoon to finalize scope?

Best regards,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
CC: Ben Carter (Sales Engineering), Jordan Blake (VP Sales)
